reasoning: Washington, DC is overwhelmingly Democratic, has no U.S. Senate representation, and is not a competitive presidential battleground; recent coverage and polling focus instead on local primaries and do not show any meaningful partisan margin comparable to D+ or R+ statewide measures.[4] Given DC’s structural partisan lean (Cook PVI of about D+86 statewide) and the absence of federal Senate races, the effective partisan margin for any federal-level contest is best characterized as safely and overwhelmingly Democratic rather than based on fresh head-to-head polling.[4] No reputable outlet in the last 45 days has published DC-specific presidential trial-heat numbers, so the structural D+86 PVI is the most relevant quantitative indicator of the current partisan margin.
